headlines.title: Lockheed Martin (LMT) Puts $10 Million Into Canada As Global Defense Deals Build
headlines.summary: Lockheed Martin (NYSE:LMT) pledged a $10 million contribution to support the launch of Canada's integrated defence ecosystem. The defence contractor reported new international agreements, including Mexico's expansion of its C-130J Super Hercules fleet. Lockheed Martin reached an F-35A delivery milestone tied to Germany's procurement program, advancing allied airpower integration.

headlines.title: Directed Energy Weapons Market Forecasts Growth from $4.58B (2026) to $12.11B by 2035, Profiling Lockheed Martin, RTX, Leidos & MBDA
headlines.summary: The directed energy weapons (DEW) market, valued at USD 4.17 billion in 2025, is projected to grow from USD 4.58 billion in 2026 to USD 12.11 billion by 2035 at an 11.4% CAGR. Growth is driven by demand for cost-effective laser and microwave systems for counter-drone, air, and missile defense. OEM-fit solutions are expected to lead by deployment, while supporting sensors, command-and-control, and integration systems will record the fastest growth.

headlines.title: Could IBM (IBM) and Lockheed Martin (LMT)’s Quantum Bet Face a Long Road to Returns?
headlines.summary: International Business Machines Corporation (NYSE:IBM) and Lockheed Martin Corporation (NYSE:LMT) have established a quantum innovation hub at ETH Zurich through an offset agreement with armasuisse, Switzerland’s Federal Office for Defence Procurement.

headlines.summary: Boeing trades at a 49.7x forward P/E versus Lockheed's 17.3x, but one carries turnaround upside while the other offers fortress-like stability.

description: Lockheed Martin Corporation, an aerospace and defense company, engages in the research, design, development, manufacture, integration, and sustainment of technology systems, products, and services in the United States, Europe, Asia, the Middle East, and internationally. The company operates through four segments: Aeronautics; Missiles and Fire Control (MFC); Rotary and Mission Systems (RMS); and Space. The Aeronautics segment offers combat and air mobility aircraft, unmanned air vehicles, and related technologies. The MFC segment provides air and missile defense systems; tactical missiles and precision strike weapon systems; logistics; fire control systems; mission operations support, readiness, engineering support, and integration services; and ground vehicles. The RMS segment offers military and commercial helicopters, surface ships, sea- and land-based missile defense systems, radar and laser systems, sea- and air-based mission and combat systems, command and control mission solutions, cyber solutions, simulation and training solutions, and services and support for surface ships. The Space segment provides satellites; space transportation systems; strategic, advanced strike, and defensive systems; and classified systems and services in support of national security systems. This segment also provides network-enabled situational awareness; and integrates space and ground global systems to help its customers gather, analyze, and securely distribute critical intelligence data. It primarily serves the U.S. government and international customers, as well as foreign military sales contracted through the U.S. government. The company was formerly known as The Lockheed Corporation and changed its name to Lockheed Martin Corporation in March 1995. Lockheed Martin Corporation was founded in 1912 and is based in Bethesda, Maryland.
